# `set_power_led_mode`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the power LED mode.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build only; not registered in the 32-bit build) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xcb200, SetPowerLedMode @0x3221e0, S50PSetPowerLedMode @0x321970 (64-bit build); vendor ASI_POWERLED_SetMode (archived library) |

Forwards an integer mode to the power-LED helper, which sets hardware mode and brightness and caches the mode. Requires an initialised power-LED handle; when uninitialised the helper logs and returns failure. Some already-current-mode paths succeed without a write. Present in the 64-bit build only; the 32-bit build has no such handler. The error text for a bad params type says expected object although an integer is required.

Side effects: Changes the power LED hardware mode and brightness and caches the mode.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_power_led_mode"`. [READ] |
| `params` | integer | yes | - | Power LED mode. Must be a bare JSON integer: no object key or array form is accepted. The handler applies no range restriction; the helper forwards the value to the vendor power-LED call (and has special handling in one internal state). With the ring-pattern LED driver modes 0 to 20 are accepted, each starting a flash, breathe or static pattern, and larger values fail as a helper failure; with the character-device driver the value is written as given. The visual meaning of each mode is unresolved. [READ (range and pass-through; vendor library from an archived copy); unresolved (meanings)] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent, null or not an integer (message says object) | `expected object param` |
| 207 | Helper returned failure and set no error code of its own (power-LED handle uninitialised or API failure); a helper-assigned code would be forwarded instead | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Which error codes the power-LED API can produce is unresolved; the helper maps no new error.

## Example

Request, set-mode - Mode value invented:

```json
{"id":40,"method":"set_power_led_mode","params":1}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_power_led_mode","result":0,"code":0,"id":40}
```

Reply, bad-params:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_power_led_mode","error":"expected object param","code":107,"id":41}
```
